newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa not budging on pay dispute.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa not budging on pay dispute.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Tuesday that it had not moved on the essential points of its 1997 wage offer during talks with the DAG white-collar trade union.
"Lufthansa made it clear that there is no room for negotiation either on the amount of payment or the length (of the contract on offer)," a Lufthansa spokeswoman said in response to enquiries.
The spokeswoman said however that the airline had shown its willingness to find agreement on job protection measures and "the long-term perspectives" of its employees.

An official for DAG, which last week organised stoppages of Lufthansa flights in protest at the airline's position, said after the talks that it was still determining its repines but said the talks had brought no "nearing of positions".

Talks between Lufthansa and the white-collar trade union, which represents sections of the airline's ground and air crew, broke down last month when Lufthansa failed to agree to the four percent wage increase being demanded by DAG.
DAG, which also objects to Lufthansa's demand that new contracts extend over a 27-month period, last week organised protests that forced 35 flights to be cancelled and more to be delayed.
DAG deputy board chairman Hubert Gartz said after the talks that the union had also not altered its demands during the talks.
"Improvements are necessary both in the level of payments on offer and the duration (of the contract)," he said in a statement released by the union.
Lufthansa last month struck a pay deal with workers represented by the OeTV public sector and transport union which involved one-off payments and a 1.7 percent wage rise through to the end of 1998.
DAG has said that the offer given to its workers would leave them with a pay rise little different to inflation.
